title: Non-blocking follow-ups from backend-portfolio-load-performance-followups-followups's PR #354 review
description: PR #354 (backend-portfolio-load-performance-followups-followups) vectorized detect_kangaroo_tails and was accepted after independent re-verification (hand-computed reference-value tests, vectorization-bug-class scrutiny, isolated-function and end-to-end speedup reproduction, dedup-fix mutation test). This tracks the review's non-blocking findings so they aren't lost once the PR merges.

checklist.step: PR #354's own `decisions` entry (checklist item 3, profiling find_divergences/find_swing_points) found that `app.signals.divergence.current_divergence` re-runs `find_swing_points` on the SAME `price` series independently for each of its 3 indicators x 2 kinds (macd_histogram/stochastic/rsi x bullish/bearish) -- 6 redundant full-history swing-point scans per ticker, measured at ~0.72s/ticker on an AAPL-scale ~11,539-row series, now the largest remaining O(history) secondary cost in a swing-mode portfolio load after this PR's kangaroo_tail fix. The task-worker judged fixing this out of scope for that task (it would mean restructuring `current_divergence`'s own call structure, e.g. a `build_divergence_swing_cache`-equivalent single price-swing-point pass shared across all 3 indicators, reusable the same way `confirmed_divergence_as_of` already reuses one) and did not file a tracked follow-up for it at the time -- recorded here instead so it isn't lost. Worth a dedicated task: share one price-swing-point pass across `current_divergence`'s 3 indicators instead of recomputing it 6 times, with its own hand-computed/mutation-tested verification per this codebase's `add-indicator`-adjacent conventions for signal-detection changes.

PR #354 review (code-review skill pass, backend/app/signals/kangaroo_tail.py + backend/app/api/routers/portfolio.py scope): in backend-portfolio-load-performance-followups-followups.json's checklist, item 4 ("If pursuing the parallelization angle instead of (or alongside) vectorization: design and implement a ProcessPoolExecutor-based...") is marked `"done": true`, but the task's own `decisions` entry explicitly states the ProcessPoolExecutor angle was NOT pursued at all (the algorithmic/vectorization angle was chosen instead). Marking a conditional, never-triggered checklist step `done: true` rather than `false` or reworded (e.g. "N/A -- angle not pursued, see decisions") is defensible (the condition that would have required action was never met) but is ambiguous enough that a future reader scanning checklist completion could misread it as "the ProcessPoolExecutor version was built." Non-blocking, documentation-only -- worth a human sanity-check / wording tweak next time that task file is touched.

decisions.decision: Fixed the find_swing_points redundancy by computing `app.signals.divergence.current_divergence`'s own PRICE swing points ONCE per call (`find_swing_points(price, window=window)`, partitioned into `lows`/`highs` lists), then feeding those same two lists into a new helper, `_latest_divergence_from_swings`, called once per supplied indicator (macd_histogram/stochastic/rsi) -- instead of each indicator's own `latest_divergence` call independently re-deriving swing points via `find_divergences` -> `swing_lows`/`swing_highs` -> a fresh `find_swing_points`. This reduces the swing-point pass count from 6 (3 indicators x 2 kinds) to 1 per `current_divergence` invocation. `_latest_divergence_from_swings` mirrors `latest_divergence`'s own tail exactly (build a bullish + bearish candidate list via `divergences_from_swings`, `max(..., key=lambda d: d.second.date)`) rather than reusing `_pick_most_recent` (a different function, built for cross-INDICATOR tie-breaking via `_INDICATOR_PRIORITY`, which doesn't apply within one indicator's own bullish-vs-bearish candidates) -- kept as a small, literal, easy-to-verify diff rather than a bigger restructuring. `latest_divergence` itself and `find_divergences` are both left completely unchanged (still public, still used directly by GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis's whole-history divergence display and by this module's own reference tests), since only `current_divergence`'s OWN internal call structure had the redundancy -- the task's own description and PR #354's finding are both specifically about `current_divergence`, not about `find_divergences`/`latest_divergence` as standalone entry points, and correctness there was already covered by the existing test suite. Did NOT reuse the existing `DivergenceSwingCache`/`build_divergence_swing_cache`/`confirmed_divergence_as_of` machinery: that trio is purpose-built for the INCREMENTAL, no-look-ahead, per-bar-of-a-growing-prefix case (`app.signals.engine.analyse_history`, one cache reused across up to thousands of per-bar calls, each needing swing points confirmable only up to that bar's own position) -- `current_divergence` is a single whole-history call with no growing-prefix/no-look-ahead concern at all, so introducing that same positional-confirmation machinery here would add unused complexity (an unconditional `position = len(price) - 1` confirmation check that can never reject anything) for no benefit over the simpler direct swing-list partition used instead.
decisions.rationale: Verification per this task's own required rigor ("verify correctness carefully... mutation-test any caching change"), matching the standard PR #354 already established: (1) ALL 35 tests in tests/unit/signals/test_divergence.py pass unchanged, including every pre-existing hand-computed-value assertion (FIXTURE_A's bullish divergence, the MACD centerline/Lovvorn-filter/aborted-divergence cases, the tie-break tests) -- these are exact hand-derived field-value assertions, not parity-only, so this alone is genuine reference-value verification of the refactored current_divergence. (2) Added 7 new tests: two using `unittest.mock.patch.object(divergence, 'find_swing_points', wraps=...)` to assert `find_swing_points` is called exactly once per `current_divergence` invocation (for 1 and for 3 supplied indicators) -- these are the tests that actually discriminate the fix from the pre-fix redundancy (see mutation-test note below); three cross-checking `current_divergence`'s per-indicator result against `latest_divergence`'s own independent (still-unfixed, still-redundant) computation for each of macd_histogram/stochastic/rsi individually, plus one isolating the bearish/`highs` branch specifically (every pre-existing current_divergence test only exercised the bullish/lows side) -- proving the shared swing lists are correctly split and correctly wired per indicator/kind, not just 'happens to work for the one fixture already covered'; two proving non-staleness across consecutive calls in the same process with genuinely different inputs (alternating bullish-only/bearish-only price series back-to-back, and the same price with two different `window` values wide enough to exclude FIXTURE_A's own known swing points) -- since this fix adds no module-level/cross-call cache (swing points are recomputed fresh at the top of every `current_divergence` call, only shared WITHIN that one call across its up to 3 indicators), there is no actual staleness mechanism possible, but these tests guard against a future regression that mistakenly introduces one. 100% line/branch coverage on the module confirmed via the full backend suite. (3) Mutation-tested the fix's OWN discriminating power directly: temporarily reverted `current_divergence`'s body to the pre-fix per-indicator-`latest_divergence` implementation (restoring the exact function body from git history afterward) and re-ran tests/unit/signals/test_divergence.py -- the 2 new call-count tests failed as expected (`spy.call_count` 0 instead of 1, since the reverted implementation never calls `find_swing_points` directly, only indirectly via `swing_lows`/`swing_highs`), while every pre-existing correctness-only test still passed, proving those correctness tests alone would NOT have caught a regression back to the redundant implementation -- exactly the gap the 2 new tests close. (4) Independently confirmed the redundancy count itself: patching `app.signals.swing_points.find_swing_points` (not `divergence.find_swing_points` -- the pre-fix implementation only calls it indirectly through `swing_lows`/`swing_highs`) around a call to the pre-fix implementation (retrieved via `git show origin/main:backend/app/signals/divergence.py`, for measurement/comparison purposes only, not shipped) confirmed exactly 6 calls for 3 supplied indicators, vs. the new implementation's confirmed 1. (5) Measured the isolated speedup on a synthetic ~11,539-row (AAPL-scale) daily series with all 3 indicator series populated (so every one of the original 6 find_swing_points calls actually executes, matching the ~0.72s/ticker figure's own scenario): pre-fix ~0.711s/call, post-fix ~0.232s/call -- a ~3.06x speedup for `current_divergence` itself given all 3 indicators supplied (a smaller multiple than a naive '6x fewer find_swing_points calls' would suggest, since `current_divergence`'s own per-indicator/per-pair evaluation work -- `_evaluate_pair`'s filters, `_is_aborted`, etc. -- is unaffected by this fix and remains real remaining cost). (6) Ran a 40-trial randomized differential fuzz test (independent of and in addition to the hand-computed suite) comparing the pre-fix (`git show origin/main`) and post-fix implementations on freshly-generated random-walk price/macd/stochastic/rsi series of varying seeds: zero field mismatches (`dataclasses.asdict` equality) across all 40 trials, including trials where either side found no divergence at all (presence-mismatch also checked, none found).

decisions.decision: For the checklist item 4 wording-ambiguity finding, edited backend-portfolio-load-performance-followups-followups.json's checklist item 4 `step` text in place (appending a bracketed clarification after the original text, not rewriting it) rather than only appending a fresh `decisions` entry pointing at the ambiguity from a distance.
decisions.rationale: This task's own checklist item 2 (immediately above) explicitly names 'a human sanity-check / wording tweak next time that task file is touched' as the resolution, with a worked example matching exactly what was applied ('N/A -- angle not pursued, see decisions') -- i.e. the checklist item itself calls out the OTHER task's existing checklist-item text as the thing to fix, which is the specific carve-out CLAUDE.md's append-only convention (for correcting a stale claim in an already-done task) allows an in-place edit under: narrow factual clarification (not a rewrite of what was actually decided -- the original 'is defensible... but is ambiguous' framing and the original step description are both left completely intact, only a bracketed addendum was appended), original text recoverable via git history, the correction is ALSO recorded as a fresh `decisions` entry on that same task (added directly to backend-portfolio-load-performance-followups-followups.json, alongside this pointer entry here), and it doesn't touch code or merge state. Only appending a decisions entry elsewhere (e.g. only here, or only as a brand-new entry on that other task without touching the ambiguous line itself) would have left the actual object of the review finding -- the checklist item's own confusing text a future reader scans -- unchanged, which defeats the point of a 'wording tweak' fix specifically (as opposed to a general decisions-log correction).
